dossier.public_summary: This 82 ppm dip looks on-target but its depth jumps from a few ppm to more than 500 ppm between sectors and between individual transits, driven by a handful of very deep events inconsistent with a planet. The odd-even mismatch and strong non-coherent variability instead favour stellar activity or a diluted eclipsing binary-like signal over a 0.79 Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes by 974.4% across sectors, alone never a planet reject but here accompanied by per-sector depth changes.
Within SPOC 2-min alone the depth is not steady; sectors with -120 ppm (sector 61) and 528 ppm (sector 33) vs 2 ppm (sector 39) show true astrophysical variation, not pipeline calibration.
Individual transits are wildly inconsistent; extreme outliers at 1436 ppm (20.9 sigma), 1147 ppm and 1054 ppm drive the folded 82 ppm signal, inconsistent with a planet.
Odd and even transits differ globally and by sector in a way that does not match a single planet at 6.66 d.
Centroid places dip on target, ruling out a neighbour EB, so the variable depth must arise on or very near the target, i.e. stellar variability or a diluted EB on the target.
